I stumbled across this fantastic app today. I love organised and clean looking notes apps and this is perfect. I've paid for pro after almost 3 hours of using it and definitely see the benefit. The Toothpaste theme is definitely a great look. 

If you're looking for a clean, stable and heavily customisable notes app. Download now and definitely go Pro! You get a weeks trial to try out the features too.

I'm always looking for the right writing app that can do it all and still be simple and unimposing. This is it. This makes me want to open the app and write in it, with the others I just forget and end up using notes instead

Positives: an elegantly designed and presented app. 

Negatives: syncing is poorly implemented, bordering on half-baked. I'm syncing between two Macs, an iPad and an iPhone. Some notes simply don't sync at all; on both iPad and iPhone, images in notes don't appear. 

Preferences/settings are minimal so there's no way of manually initiating a sync. It may be automatic, but if one can't trust the sync, one can't trust the app. 

Finally, this requires an annual subscription for iCloud syncing and themes. Given that iCloud syncing is an Apple-provided technology the fact that these guys are charging is a disgrace. 

I've seen a few people talking about this being 1) an Evernote killer; 2) a Ulysses killer. On the first point, Bear handles attachments and webpage rendering more poorly than Apple Notes does, so if it can't kill Notes it's hardly worrying Evernote. Evernote is hideous, so I await a proper app into which I can import my old Evernote library. 

Anyone who thinks this is a Ulysses killer is an idiot, having been duped by the superficial likeness of the apps. Ulysses is better-designed with a rock-solid syncing backend. It is also has infinitely superior document management (by which I mean it actually has document management) and export options. But to be fair to the Bear guys, they don't mention Ulysses so the comparison is unfair. 

I'm giving it until the end of my free month to see if an update improves the performance of this app, but at this stage, I'm afraid it's hype over substance. Ho-hum.

Having read some of the reviews of Bear, I chose to try it and was really surprised. It's a great app and allows focus on writing but then also to mark effectively.

The layouts are clean, fonts are effective and ability to add order to content is fantastic. 

I wasn't put off by the annual subscription as some are saying as I figured the cost was less than I spend on coffee in a week, so I either spend too much on coffee, or others expect great things for free.

Found this app after a review by the magnificent Federico Viticci at MacStories - this is a well thought out and versatile note taking app. 

It's based in Markdown which is simple and easy to use and learn, basically it's fancy plain text, however like the 'green elephant' it also handles pdfs/ doc files etc. It's more versatile than the built in Notes app, although it doesn't (as yet) have a drawing or a reminders/ alarm facility (which would be nice.... Devs if you're reading this...) There's a Pro version for a couple of quid a month that gives you more export options and some nice themes, although the basic free app is pretty viable but itself - however I went Pro immediately because, after all, this is not a charity and the devs will need €€ to keep going. 

Well worth it and hope it sticks around!

The Bear team let me be a beta tester for this app and so I've been using it for a while now. On release I had no hesitation: I installed and bought a pro subscription immediately.

I've used many notes apps and Markdown editors. Evernote is highly functional but its formatting is weird and the interface is clunky and inconsistent. SimpleNote is great but just lacks functionality. Byword is a beautiful editor but lacks any organisational mechanism. 

Bear takes the best of all of these: beautiful Markdown editing; a clever tagging system; sophisticated search; an interface that's not in-your-face. It's a joy.

My only issue is small, but not insignificant: it's tied to Apple's devices and infrastructure when I'd prefer a more cross-platform solution.

Nearly perfect. Great job on the release!
